svg.title: Why four checks all missed a bug in the shipped app
svg.desc: In development the dev server resolves bare package names itself, so a dynamic import written as a runtime string works on every machine it is tried on. In the built app the same string is handed to the webview to resolve as a URL, which fails, because there is no package directory inside a Mac app. Type checking, linting, the test suite and continuous integration all read the source rather than the built output, so none of them could see it. A check that scans the built chunks and fails the build now closes the gap.
svg.text: The dev server resolves the package name itself
Works. On every machine, every time.
The webview is asked for a URL, and has none
Fails. Six of seven languages, every copy.
Four checks, all reading the same side of the build
Ask every check one question: does it look at the artefact, or at the source it came from? Only one of those is what your users get.
